interpretations.text: For declared breaks, a reason that the existing clinical screen classifies CLINICAL (clinical category, clinical flag or clinical mention) is, from the moment it is recorded, a clinical restriction in the sense of AEC §7, not a correctable context flag. Its correction to a nonclinical reason by the athlete is recorded as the athlete's statement and never releases the clinical route. AEC §7's 'Correção pode resolver um flag de contexto incorreto' keeps applying to every nonclinical context fact of a break: dates, length, start time, a nonclinical category changed for another, free text the screen does not classify CLINICAL, and an unclear (ASK) reason clarified.
interpretations.whyWithinAuthority: It chooses, between the two halves of AEC §7, the one the current explicit Founder decision and G04 already select for clinical causes; it adds no number, input, field, criterion or dose; it moves the runtime only toward the existing clinical hold.
interpretations.promotion: Record-level reading bound to R7-D. If it is ever written into AEC, PDR or the index, that is a doctrine change through the PCG product_doctrine branch (independent Research audit and Product/UX interpretability review, Chief consolidation) at an authorized canon sync.

interpretations.text: In the R7-D interface, the clearance continuation (§5.4, INTERFACE-3) covers a clinical route that a qualified human cleared while the kept break's own reason is nonclinical (a current clinical flag, a substitution with pain). A return from a break whose own reason is clinical is clinical return, out of scope (§1) until G04 exists. Inside the synthetic shadow evaluation the clearance step models a qualified human; it is not a product mechanism (PCG-F08-O02).

rulings.question: P-1
rulings.summary: Does any current authority permit implementing S5 (clearance recorded) or S6 (sporting reassessment and progressive return) now, in whole or in part?
rulings.ruling: NOT_IMPLEMENTABLE_UNDER_CURRENT_AUTHORITY for S5 and S6, in whole and in part, including an inert, record-only clearance fact
rulings.form: BLOCKED_BY_AUTHORITY; the proposal is recorded as the candidate handed to the G04 owners and Security (see proposalAdmissibility). Only S3 hardening is implementable now.
reasons: S5's content is G04's: issuer classes, verification, scope codes, restriction vocabulary, stop signs, validity and expiry are 'classes concretas ... elegibilidade, restrição, liberação' that the G04 row reserves to competent professionals. No G04 owner exists. A schema written without them would invent clinical authority.

Even a fact that is recorded and never read is collection of a clinical fact and a new input across a trust boundary: G04 ('Antes de coletar/classificar/atuar'), G07 (before collection or persistence) and the Phase 3.4 Security condition apply first. An inert placeholder would also signal an exit that does not exist.

S6 is a return after a clinical cause. G04 reserves 'liberação e retorno' to competent professionals; DR-99 keeps clinical return CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; SSCTR-05 forbids the SSCTR to approve it. The SSCTR can define the sporting content only inside a scope and a return framework a G04 owner has approved.
S6 cannot exist before S5: every S6 entry condition depends on a valid clearance fact.
implementableNow: R-F08-1 (S3 hardening; see P-4), under the Phase 3.4 authorization and its conditions.

S3 characterization tests that need no clearance input (proposal §7): clinical condition active; no clearance; a trip or holiday trying to overwrite the clinical cause; an athlete reclassification attempt (named correction, before and after a clinical route, during it, after a client clearance); history preserved; another event's change never applied with a clinical decision.
Disclosures in the freeze, handoff, interface and pre-registration (append-only).
proposalOnly: The SSCTR's Part 1 Q8 answer (the sporting process after a legitimate clearance): an offline proposal for a future joint G04/SSCTR review. It is not runtime authority and approves no clinical return.

rulings.question: P-2
rulings.summary: What makes a clearance qualified, and may an athlete-declared clearance ever open S6?
rulings.ruling: Governance definition decided (content G04's). Athlete-issued clearance: NOT_ADMISSIBLE under current authority, ever. A professional's clearance relayed by the athlete: NOT_ADMISSIBLE now; only the G04 owners with Security/Privacy and G07 could ever admit it as a provenance level.
rulings.form: Form requirements Q-1 to Q-8 below are within PCG's authority (they restate G04, AEC, AEOS and PDM). Their content belongs to the G04 owners and is BLOCKED_BY_AUTHORITY.

qualifiedClearance.text: Issuer: a real, identifiable human professional whose class is on a G04-approved list for that cause and scope (a physician where clinical evaluation is needed; any other class only as G04 approves). The athlete, the coach, the SSCTR, an LLM, a score, a wearable signal or elapsed time is never an issuer.

Verification: a level approved by G04 with Security/Privacy (and G07 for the data). The engine never validates a medical document, never reads a clearance from free text or an image, and never infers one ('texto "profissional aprovou" não vale approval record', HC02).
Binding: it names the clinical episode it clears, of this athlete, and is issued on or after that episode began. It is never transferred to another episode, athlete or later sign.

Scope: per sport (RUN, STRENGTH), each cleared, restricted or not cleared, with restrictions only from a closed G04-approved vocabulary. The engine never reads free text as a restriction. A restriction is a hard cap no profile overrides.
Validity: issued on a date, valid forward only (AEC 'sem clearance retroativo'), with a review or expiry rule set by G04. It is not withdrawn or contradicted, and no clinical sign has appeared since.
Exit signs: G04-approved stop signs send the athlete back to S3.
Record: an append-only fact of its own. It never edits, replaces or reclassifies the clinical declaration, whose reason stays recorded.
Necessary, never sufficient: a current eligibility re-answer (NONCLINICAL_CONFIRMED, every flag false) is still required before S6, but on its own it never opens S5 or S6.

athleteDeclared.selfIssued: An athlete-issued clearance ('I feel fine', 'I am ready', RECOVERED, an eligibility re-answer, a checkbox, a correction or a later report) never opens S6. It is a confirmation, which G04 excludes ('Confirmação ... não dão clearance'); AEC excludes release by a 'checkbox de risco'; AEOS forbids asking the user for clearance; PS04 forbids filling G04 with acceptance. Changing this would be a Founder doctrine change against DR-99 and G04, plus legal service-model review. It is not available, not requested and not recommended here.
athleteDeclared.relayedProfessionalClearance: An athlete entering a named professional's clearance is a provenance question, not self-clearance. It is not admissible now, and the proposal's 'ATHLETE_DECLARED opens S6 only if G04 and Security approve' is the right owner split. Whether such a relay can ever be an admissible verification level, for which classes and scopes, is OPEN_QUESTION PCG-F08-Q03. PCG does not decide it.

rulings.question: P-3
rulings.summary: Until G04 has an owner, is an interim exit acceptable, such as a fresh onboarding after the professional's clearance (benchmark RN1), or would it bypass the clinical boundary?
rulings.ruling: NOT_ADMISSIBLE: it bypasses the clinical boundary. No interim exit exists under current authority.
rulings.form: Applies existing canon; no new rule. The interim state is S3/S4, defined below.
reasons: An honest fresh onboarding gives no exit: a clinical pause reason at intake routes to a human (r6-intake.mjs lines 177-178 and 191), the same boundary as F08.

A fresh onboarding gives a plan only if the athlete omits or relabels the cause, or if the new program does not read the kept clinical episode. The first is the athlete reclassifying the original cause; the second lets a later act erase an earlier injury. The Founder forbids both.

A plan after a clinical hold is 'liberar hold ou prescrever retorno', which G04 reserves to competent professionals. The professional's clearance would be neither recorded nor verified: the plan would rest on the athlete's word that it happened (see P-2).

The benchmark shows competitors leave the decision to the user and a professional, with a disclaimer. A competitor having a feature is not authority to adopt it (PCG constitution). The benchmark itself classes the self-managed patterns 4, 5 and 12 as REJECT for clinical causes, and RN1 as ADAPT only as the G04-subject target.
interimState: S3/S4: CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; no prescription; the record keeps accepting evidence and the athlete may keep logging.

The hold carries its owner (a qualified human), next step (qualified assessment outside the product) and exit evidence (a future G04 clearance fact), as PDM requires; the exit evidence is undefined until G04.
No stale plan presented as current; no growth pressure (DR-125); no 'start a new plan' or 'change the reason' offered as an exit; routing copy only under G04 (clinical copy not finalized).
A new user's onboarding is unaffected: the existing intake gate applies.

classification.normative: CURRENT_PRODUCT_DECISION, coaching-policy layer; MUST (outcome only; how the runtime achieves it is Engineering's design space)

restriction.text: The clinical status of a declared break belongs to its episode, not to the report in force. If any report of an episode on record was classified CLINICAL by the existing interruption screen, on any basis (clinical category, clinical flag or clinical mention), the episode is a clinical-cause episode at every later decision, whatever a later report of it states. An episode's reports are those joined by the existing episode semantics: a name, or the same facts. A named correction of such an episode is still recorded append-only and still corrects its other facts (dates, length, start time, text). Its nonclinical reason is kept as the athlete's statement. It never removes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, never opens a nonclinical return and never sets a return class. This holds whether or not a clinical route was issued before the correction, whether the correction was sent during a clinical route or after a client clearance, and on every path that reads the episode (a weekly review, a return report, an answer, a separate-break read). An episode whose reports the screen classified only ASK or NONCLINICAL is unaffected: clarifying an unclear reason stays a correction.

residuals.text: A mistaken clinical category or flag holds the athlete in CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, with no exit in the product until a G04 owner exists. This fails closed and follows the canon. The cost is real: one mistaken entry ends the athlete's plan in the product. It is the Founder's to weigh against the reopening trigger (funding a G04 owner), not PCG's to relax.
residuals.mitigation: Consumer design space (Product/UX): confirm a clinical category or flag with the athlete before the report is sent; plain routing copy under G04. The runtime does not change for it.

residuals.text: A free-text mention the screen reads as clinical, in a report with a nonclinical category (an idiom, for example), also becomes permanent. Whether a mention-only classification can be a correctable misread is a G04 triage question (PCG-F08-Q02). The interim reading fails closed.

whyNotTheAlternatives: Keep the path and only disclose it: the Founder's Phase 3.4 decision forbids it, and G04 and AEC exclude release by athlete confirmation.

Allow the correction only before a clinical route is issued: the window exists only through an incidental ordering (PCG-F08-O01), and the stated cause is already a clinical signal (SSCTR-05). It would still be the athlete reclassifying.
Allow it within some time window: that is a new number, outside authority.
Remove corrections of clinical-cause breaks entirely: unnecessary, because dates, length and text stay correctable without touching the clinical status.

blocker.statement: F08 (no legitimate exit after a break whose own reason is clinical) is BLOCKED_BY_AUTHORITY. The exit needs a clearance fact (S5) and a post-clearance return framework (S6). Both need the G04 competent qualified professionals, a physician where clinical evaluation is needed, to approve: issuer classes, verification, scope, restriction vocabulary, stop signs, validity, and whether and how a clinical-cause episode may be rebuilt. No such owner exists in the project. Security/Privacy and G07 must also approve the clearance input before it enters the runtime, and the legal service model must say who may clear. Until then the athlete stays in CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED (S3/S4): the record keeps accepting evidence, no plan is given, and no interim exit exists. R-F08-1 closes the athlete-reclassification path and does not resolve F08.

conditions.text: No S5 or S6 in the runtime: no clearance input, field, flag, event kind or client convention a consumer would rely on, inert or not, until G04, Security/Privacy and G07 approve and a Founder mission authorizes it.

No athlete statement ends a clinical-cause episode. That covers 'I feel fine', RECOVERED, an eligibility re-answer, a return report, a correction, a fresh onboarding, a later break, elapsed time, executed training and a count of weeks.

If R-F08-1 is implemented in Phase 3.4: (a) RED on R7D-FREEZE-4 for the P1, P3 and T5 shapes, GREEN after; (b) no new number, input, field or screen vocabulary; (c) r7d-phase32 T5's assertion changes only as a marked update that the SSCTR and Quality narrow checks accept, never silently; (d) append-only INTERFACE and PREREG deltas supersede INTERFACE-4's 'one exception' and PREREG-4 Δ12 before any holdout; (e) SSCTR and Quality narrow checks on the candidate; (f) residuals R-F08-R1/R2 disclosed; (g) F08 stays open.

If R-F08-1 is not implemented before the next freeze: the freeze and handoff carry PCG-F08-F01 as an open DOWNSTREAM_VIOLATION. F08 is described as 'fail-closed except an athlete-statement exit that the Founder's current decision forbids', never as plain fail-closed or resolved. No consumer may expose a reason correction for a clinical-cause episode.
F08_OPEN in every case: never declared resolved. KNOWN_FAIL_CLOSED_AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY stays, qualified by C03 or C04.

For any future consumer (owner Product/UX with Data; no UI in this mission): never drop or replace the clinical continuation state, since no clearance mechanism exists. Never present the stale plan as current under a clinical route. No growth pressure (DR-125). Never offer 'start a new plan' or 'change the reason' as an exit. Route plainly to a qualified human, with clinical copy only under G04. Keep recording. Never expose the cause socially.

The interface's QUALIFIED_CLEARANCE step stays an evaluation-client convention modelling a qualified human in synthetic shadow cases (I-F08-2). It is not a product mechanism, not a runtime input and not evidence that an exit exists.

The SSCTR's Part 1 Q8 answer is an offline proposal for a future joint G04/SSCTR review. It approves no clinical return and is not runtime authority. If it conflicts with this record on the authority form, the conflict returns to PCG and the Chief; neither silently prevails.
No product/, canon/, mission, ledger or queue edit by this record. The canon note is a proposal only.
